title: Marcos: Self-restraint, mutual respect key to peaceful dispute resolution
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday said the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China should uphold self-restraint, mutual respect and practical cooperation as they mark the 50th…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday said the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China should uphold self-restraint, mutual respect and practical cooperation as they mark the 50th anniversary of the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC).

"During this anniversary year, our shared commitment to international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes must be reflected in our actions, including through self-restraint, mutual respect, and practical cooperation," Marcos said in his opening remarks at the ASEAN-China Summit.
The TAC serves as ASEAN's legally binding agreement and code of conduct governing interstate relations among member states and countries in the region.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang said China remained committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade with ASEAN countries.

"Although economic and trade restrictions have substantially increased around the world, we remain firmly committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade, and endeavor to make the pie of cooperation bigger," Li said in his opening remarks.
China acceded to the TAC in 2003.
Meanwhile, member states are expected to review ASEAN-China relations and discuss the next steps for cooperation during the 29th ASEAN-China Summit.— MCG, GMA News
